We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (likely okay). Need to construct route using templates.

We have some templates found: reaction_id 723274 is sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine (Cl-C(=O)-aryl? Wait template: Cl-C(=O)-[c] + [#7:4]-[SH] -> sulfonamide? Actually retro: product is sulfonamide, reactants are aryl acyl chloride and sulfenamide? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: [#7:4]-[S;H0;D4;+0:5](=O)(=O)-[c]>>Cl-C(=O)-[c] + [#7:4]-[SH](=O)=O . So forward reaction: aryl acyl chloride + sulfenamide -> sulfonamide? Not typical. Might be mis.

But we can use simpler: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide (common). Need template for that. Search for sulfonamide formation with sulfonyl chloride. Let's search functional_groups_broken: acyl chloride, formed: sulfonamides. Already did but got empty. Maybe need functional_groups_broken: "acyl chloride" and formed: "sulfonamides". It returned empty earlier for simple phenyl sulfonamide? Actually we tried with Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 and got empty. Maybe template not present.

Alternative: we can break the sulfonamide bond via retrosynthesis: disconnection between N and S, giving sulfonyl chloride and amine. Could use template 723274 which seems to do that: product sulfonamide -> reactants: aryl acyl chloride (Cl-C(=O)-aryl) and sulfenamide (NH-SH?). Not ideal.

But we could propose route: 1) Form sulfonamide by reacting sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) with aniline (para-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride could be made from sulfonylation of aryl bromide? Actually sulfonyl chloride can be commercially available: e.g., p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1. That's commercially available (we saw is_buyable true). Good.

Our target sulfonamide: p-tolyl-NH-SO2-aryl (where aryl is phenyl with side chain). So we can use TsCl (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) + aniline derivative (the other aryl amine). The other aryl amine is c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (a phenyl with a side chain). That aryl amine is an aniline (has NH attached to aromatic). Actually the side chain includes an amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So the aryl amine is an aniline with a side chain containing an amide and an aniline at the end. So we need that aryl amine as a leaf.

We can get that aryl amine via amide formation between acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl bromide) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N is a cinnamoyl amide attached to an aniline (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is p-phenylenediamine? It's an aniline with an extra NH2 at para? The SMILES Nc3ccccc3N is aniline with an extra NH2 at para? Actually aniline is c1ccccc1N. Nc3ccccc3N is aniline with an extra N at position 1? That's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). So the amide attaches to one of the amines, leaving the other free.

Thus we can propose: Step 1: Form amide via coupling of acryloyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=CC1=CC=CC=C1? Wait acryloyl chloride is ClC(=O)C=C). But we need a phenyl attached to the double bond: /C=C/ attached to phenyl? Actually the side chain is phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the double bond is attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(C=C... )cc2). So we need to attach a cinnamoyl amide to the phenyl ring via a Heck-type? Actually the double bond is conjugated to phenyl: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. This could be formed via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acrylamide? Or via Wittig? Simpler: we can start from 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodo) and do Heck with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). But we need commercially available acrylamide derivative: maybe N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (NH2-Ph-CO-CH=CH2). That may not be commercial.

Alternative: we could form the double bond via condensation (Knoevenagel) between benzaldehyde and malonic acid derivative? Might be complex.

Given limited time, maybe propose a 2-step route: 1) sulfonamide formation using TsCl and aryl amine (which already contains the side chain). 2) The aryl amine can be obtained by amide formation between acryloyl chloride and p-phenylenediamine (or aniline). Actually we need the aryl amine with side chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. This can be made by reacting acryloyl chloride with p-phenylenediamine (one amine reacts, other remains). That yields the desired aryl amine (the phenyl attached to double bond is the acryloyl part? Wait acryloyl chloride is CH2=CH-COCl. Reaction with p-phenylenediamine gives CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. That's the side chain but missing the phenyl attached to the double bond (the phenyl is the acryloyl part? Actually acryloyl is CH2=CH-CO-, not phenyl. Our side chain has phenyl-CH=CH-CO-. So we need cinnamoyl chloride (Ph-CH=CH-COCl). That's commercially available? Possibly "cinnamoyl chloride". Check buyability.
